precedents.note: Both applicants owe unpaid federal income taxes linked to unfiled returns and carry delinquent consumer debts, including credit card and charged-off or collection-type accounts. Both also work for a defense contractor.

Both involve applicants with unresolved delinquent debts and a federal tax debt, including a federal tax lien and an IRS payment arrangement, and both have applicants who made monthly payments on some debts without documenting the balances or payments. Both also describe debts the applicant believed were paid but could not verify with documentation.

Both applicants have delinquent federal income tax debts, including tax year 2006 in the precedent and unpaid income taxes for years in the case under review. Both also turned to a tax resolution service for help, and the precedent applicant is paying on an IRS debt through monthly payments and an Offer in Compromise.

Both applicants carry multiple delinquent debts alleged on the SOR, including federal tax debts and collection accounts, and both made some payment arrangements with creditors and the IRS while leaving several debts unverified. Both also have a federal tax lien and an IRS repayment plan at issue, and both had their financial problems tied to income loss.

Both involve Guideline F financial allegations centered on unpaid taxes, including a federal tax lien and failures to file federal income tax returns. Both applicants also claimed they were working out payment arrangements with the government over those tax debts, and each disputed some of the alleged amounts or claims.
